senses.gloss:
‘caṭaṅ’
vedic. p.. (Malayalam ?). Brahmasva Maṭha 42. 52. 121. 168. Krāṅgāṭ Mana 138. 140 (Bṛhat). 145.

‘caturbhāṇī’
title given to a collection of four Bhāṇas--(1) Ubhayābhisārikā of Vararuci, (2) Dhūrtaviṭasam3vāda of Īśvaradatta, (3) Pādatāḍitaka of Śyāmilaka an. (4) Padmaprābhṛtaka of Śūdraka. MT. 2725. 2726. For mss. etc. see under separate works.
For general studies on the four Bhāṇas see F. W. Thomas, JRAS. 1923, Centenary Supplement, p.. 123-36; S. K. D., JRAS. 1926, p.. 63-90; J. R. A. Loman, Adyar Library Bulletin. XXV. p.. 173-87. The authors of the four Bhāṇas are mentioned together a. the end of Viṭanidrā, MT. 3755.
Pt.. (1) Dakṣiṇa Bhāratī Series 1, Madras, 1922. (2) Ed. by Motichandra an. V. S. Agrawala, Śṛṅgārahāṭa, Hindi Grantharatnakar Karyalaya, Delhi, 1959. with Hindi transl.

‘candrāvalīcarita_Nāṭaka’
Skt. version of Pkt. drama. RASB. VII. 5373.

‘cārvākaṣaṣṭi’
a modern compilation of fragments of citations of the Cārvāka school from several works. by Daksinaranjan Sastrin.
Pt.. Calcutta, 1928.
